text:
**Best pick for most people: Anker SOLIX C1000 + 200W panel — about $740.** It pairs a 1,056Wh LiFePO₄ battery with 1,800W of AC output, a solid all-around size for camping and essential outage loads. It’s rated a top sub-$1,000 kit by [PWice](https://www.pwice.com/best-solar-generators-under-1000-dollars/); the listed price comes from [Dealectric’s kit comparison](https://dealectric.com/solar-generator-with-panels-included).

Other good options:

- **Best panel value: ALLPOWERS P1800 + 400W panel — about $731.** Same roughly 1kWh battery class, but twice the panel wattage of many bundles—useful if faster solar recharging matters. [See the kit](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-p1800-sp037-solar-kit).
- **Best familiar-brand alternative: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic + 220W panel — about $699.** It has a 1,024Wh battery and 1,800W output; [TechRadar’s deal coverage](https://www.techradar.com/pro/ecoflows-delta-3-solar-generator-bundle-gets-a-usd300-price-drop-at-amazon-with-the-portable-power-station-and-220w-solar-panel-built-for-camping-home-backup-and-emergencies) also notes fast wall charging and UPS switching.
- **Best lightweight option: Jackery Solar Generator 1000 v2 — about $699.** It offers 1,070Wh and 1,500W output in a reported 23 lb unit, with a 200W panel. [See the comparison](https://dealectric.com/solar-generator-with-panels-included).

**Bottom line:** I’d choose the **Anker** for a balanced, reputable all-rounder; choose **ALLPOWERS** if getting more solar panel for the money is your priority. Prices can change, so check the current total before buying.
